findings.title: Ticket-card bulk selection nests a checkbox and a status button inside a Link, so ticking a ticket also navigates
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:191-192 — the entire ticket card is a Next.js <Link href={`/admin/tickets/${ticket.id}`}>

apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:197-204 — the per-row <input type="checkbox" aria-label="Select ticket"> is rendered inside that Link; handleCheckboxChange (:184-187) only stops propagation of the change event, not the click that bubbles to the anchor

apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:218-221 — the status pill <button> inside the same Link calls handleStatusClick (:172-177) which does e.preventDefault()+e.stopPropagation(); the author guarded the button but not the checkbox
apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:551-574 — the header 'Select all on page' checkbox lives in a plain <label> outside any Link, so only per-row selection is affected

apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:21,89-111 — /admin/tickets is in the default 25-route axe gate (critical/serious only); axe's nested-interactive rule targets exactly this pattern (medium confidence it fires on the populated page)
findings.impact: Mouse users cannot multi-select tickets without navigating away (clicking a checkbox follows the card link), and the DOM nests interactive controls inside a link, which is invalid HTML and is announced/operated inconsistently by assistive tech. The bulk-update bar therefore depends on an interaction that does not work as intended.
findings.recommendation: Move the checkbox and the status control out of the Link (card as a div with a title-only link or a stretched-link overlay) or add an onClick that calls preventDefault/stopPropagation on the controls. Add a Playwright regression test that clicks the row checkbox and asserts the URL is unchanged and the selection count updates.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Static review only (no browser run); click-bubbling behaviour is inferred from the missing preventDefault on the checkbox and its presence on the sibling button, and from the f0d79194 a11y commit that resized the same checkbox without catching the nesting.

findings.title: Inline async action errors are not announced by assistive tech in ~44 components, contradicting the documented convention
evidence: docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:51-52 — 'Announce async errors with role="alert" / role="status"; associate field errors with aria-invalid + aria-describedby'
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/dmarc-coach/DmarcAnalyzeForm.tsx:93 — {error && {error}} with no live region

apps/web/components/admin/CreateRoleForm.tsx:107 and components/admin/RecordDetail.tsx:166 — server-action failures rendered as plain

with no role
apps/web/app/(public)/upload/[token]/UploadForm.tsx:62-72 — both the error and the success message for the public upload flow are unannounced
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/ai-triage/PortalTriageClient.tsx:98 and app/(portal)/portal/camera-calculator/CameraCalculatorClient.tsx:148 — portal examples

Repo-wide scan: 31 role="alert" and 15 role="status" usages, 10 files use useToast(); 44 files with an `error` state rendered in JSX have no role=alert/status/aria-live within the render block (examples above plus app/(admin)/admin/qbr/new/QbrGenerateForm.tsx:82, app/(admin)/admin/proposals/new/ProposalForm.tsx:83, components/admin/OrganizationOnboardingWizard.tsx:179)
findings.impact: A screen-reader user submitting a server action that fails receives no feedback at all (WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages, AA). Sighted users see the red text; AT users are left on the form with no indication the action failed.
findings.recommendation: Adopt a single InlineError primitive with role="alert" (or route action failures through useToast().pushToast('error', ...)), then sweep the ~44 call sites. Add a lint rule or code-review checklist item for new error renders.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Count is a static heuristic (error state rendered in JSX with no live-region attribute in the surrounding block); a handful may announce through a parent region, so treat 44 as an upper bound.

findings.title: Several dialogs have no max-height or internal scroll, so tall forms are clipped on small viewports
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/promotions/PromoForm.tsx:60-71 — 10 form controls, container 'fixed inset-0 z-50 flex items-center justify-center' with no max-h/overflow on the panel
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/categories/CategoryForm.tsx:52-63 — same pattern (5 controls + textarea)
apps/web/components/portal/SupportCenterClient.tsx:216-225 — create-ticket modal, no max-h/overflow
apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx:1769-1780 — create-document modal (max-w-3xl, multi-field form), no max-h/overflow
packages/ui/src/components/Dialog.tsx:114-119 — the shared Dialog panel is 'overflow-hidden' with no max-h, used by components/portal/DocumentShareClient.tsx:181-215

Contrasting good patterns: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/products/ProductForm.tsx:85 ('max-h-[90vh] ... overflow-y-auto'), apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/projects/AdminProjectsClient.tsx:305 and components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:718 (overlay 'items-start ... overflow-y-auto')
findings.impact: On phones or short windows the dialog can extend past the viewport and its top/bottom (including submit and cancel buttons) becomes unreachable because neither the panel nor the fixed overlay scrolls. Mobile users can be blocked from completing create/edit flows.
findings.recommendation: Add 'max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto' (or the overlay-scroll pattern) to every dialog, and fix the shared @mct/ui Dialog once so DocumentShareClient inherits it. Add a Playwright viewport test (e.g. 375x667) that opens each modal and asserts the submit button is visible.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Verified statically: modal containers lack max-h/overflow-y while three other modals in the same app already implement it, so this is an inconsistency as much as a bug.

findings.title: 89 of 319 pages have no page-specific title (79 dynamic detail pages + 10 static), so browser and AT titles are generic
evidence: Static scan of apps/web/app/**/page.tsx: 89 files export neither `metadata` nor `generateMetadata`; 79 are dynamic ([id]) routes

Dynamic examples: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx, app/(portal)/portal/support/[ticketId]/page.tsx, app/(admin)/admin/assets/[id]/page.tsx — none sets a title, so they inherit apps/web/app/layout.tsx:19-20 title 'Maine CyberTech Portal'

Static examples: app/(public)/login/page.tsx, app/(public)/signup/page.tsx, app/(public)/pending/page.tsx, app/(public)/password-reset/page.tsx, app/(public)/forgot-password/page.tsx — no title override, so they inherit the marketing default from app/(public)/layout.tsx:15-18 ('Maine CyberTech | Managed IT, Cybersecurity & Business Technology Support')
apps/web/components/RouteAnnouncer.tsx:20-23 — client-side navigation announcements fall back to document.title when no h1 is found, so the generic title propagates to the announcement
findings.impact: WCAG 2.4.2 (Page Titled, Level A) intent is not met on ~28% of routes: tabs, history and screen-reader page identification all read the same generic title, and detail pages are indistinguishable from each other.
findings.recommendation: Add generateMetadata to detail routes (ticket subject, asset/record name, org name) and explicit titles for the five auth pages. Add a test that walks the route table and asserts a non-default title per route (the existing scripts/check-docs-counts.mjs already parses route counts and could host the check).
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Counts from a static scan of page.tsx files (319 total); redirect-only pages among the 89 are not excluded from the count, but the sampled dynamic pages render real content.

findings.title: @mct/ui primitives are largely bypassed: 6 files import Button, 1 uses Input/Dialog/Badge, while the app hand-rolls 234 raw cyber-button* usages and four Chip copies
evidence: packages/ui/src/index.ts:14-21 exports Button, Input/Textarea, Badge, Avatar, Dialog, Skeleton* and SidebarGroup/Item

Usage scan across apps/web (510 tsx files): Button imported in 6 files (5 auth pages + components/portal/DocumentShareClient.tsx:5); Input, Dialog and Badge each only in DocumentShareClient.tsx:6-8; Skeleton in 25 loading.tsx files; Avatar, SidebarGroup, SidebarItem, SkeletonText, SkeletonCard, SkeletonTable have zero app usages

Raw utility classes across apps/web: cyber-button 79, cyber-button-secondary 152, cyber-button-sm 2, cyber-button-danger 1 (234 total), e.g. components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:706-710 and components/admin/RecordDetail.tsx:167-174

Duplicated local primitives: Chip defined four times — components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:254, components/admin/AdminUsersClient.tsx:25, app/(admin)/admin/projects/AdminProjectsClient.tsx:39, components/admin/AdminOrganizationsClient.tsx:113; mobile drawer shells duplicated in components/layout/SidebarShell.tsx and components/store/StoreLayoutShell.tsx
findings.impact: Shared focus, contrast, target-size and ARIA fixes have to be re-applied per call site (the f0d79194 a11y commit touched individual files for exactly this reason), and the two component sets drift. New engineers cannot tell whether @mct/ui or raw cyber-* classes are the standard.
findings.recommendation: Pick one standard and enforce it: adopt Button/Input/Dialog in a pilot module and move Chip/ConfirmDialog/StatusPill into @mct/ui, or document that raw cyber-* utilities are the standard and delete the unused exports. Add a lint guard for new raw cyber-button* usages in new files.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Counts from grep over apps/web/app + apps/web/components; loading.tsx files legitimately use Skeleton, so the 'bypass' claim is about interactive primitives.

findings.title: Four Chip copies render a glyph-only '×' remove button with a sub-24px target size
evidence: components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:254-265, components/admin/AdminUsersClient.tsx:25-35, app/(admin)/admin/projects/AdminProjectsClient.tsx:39-49, components/admin/AdminOrganizationsClient.tsx:113-126 — identical Chip implementations
Each remove button is className='ml-0.5 text-emerald-400 hover:text-emerald-200' (no padding/size classes) with content '×' and no aria-label
Chips render when list filters are active (e.g. AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:384-406, AdminUsersClient.tsx:107-130), i.e. in the populated filtered state
findings.impact: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (Target Size, AA): the hit area is roughly the 12px glyph, below the 24x24 CSS px minimum. Screen readers announce only 'times' rather than 'Remove <filter>'. The a11y gate does not catch it because the E2E scan never applies a filter (chips are not rendered).
findings.recommendation: Single Chip component in the design system with aria-label={`Remove ${label}`} and a min-h-6 min-w-6 (24px) hit area; delete the three copies.

findings.title: Theme is documented dark-only but ships dead light/system code paths (CSS variables, ThemeProvider, Storybook toolbar)
evidence: docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:83 — 'The theme is dark-only; ThemeProvider is pinned (defaultTheme="dark")'

packages/ui/src/styles.css:154-165 — defines :root[data-theme="dark"] and :root[data-theme="light"] variable sets; :28-29 .cyber-page-bg hardcodes bg-[#0A1118] text-slate-50, so the light variables would not change the page background anyway
packages/ui/src/hooks/use-theme.tsx:37-47 resolves 'system' via prefers-color-scheme and supports light; apps/web/app/layout.tsx:43 pins defaultTheme="dark" storageKey="mct-theme-dark"
grep over apps/web: 0 useTheme consumers and 0 'dark:' variant classes; no theme toggle UI exists
.storybook/preview.tsx:35-46 declares a light/dark/system toolbar that the decorator (:26-34) never reads — the toolbar is decorative
findings.impact: Dead configuration and UI affordances mislead maintainers and Storybook users into thinking a theme switch exists; a user who manually sets the localStorage key to 'light' gets an inconsistent half-themed page.
findings.recommendation: Either delete the light/system branches, the light CSS block and the Storybook toolbar, or implement a real toggle (and fix cyber-page-bg to use the variable). Whichever is chosen, keep docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:83 in sync.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; the previous run had no UX rows on theming.

findings.title: Sidebar group toggles declare aria-haspopup='true' for a popup that is a link list, not a menu
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/AdminSidebarContent.tsx:104 and components/portal/PortalSidebarContent.tsx:104 — aria-haspopup="true" on the group toggle buttons
The controlled popup (AdminSidebarContent.tsx:125-171) is a plain <div> of <Link> elements with no role=menu/menuitem; aria-expanded and aria-controls are already correct
Keyboard handling exists (ArrowDown opens + focuses the first link, Escape closes: AdminSidebarContent.tsx:46-68), so only the popup-type announcement is wrong
findings.impact: ARIA mismatch: aria-haspopup="true" is equivalent to menu and makes screen readers announce a menu that does not exist, while the disclosure semantics already convey the state correctly.
findings.recommendation: Remove aria-haspopup (keep aria-expanded + aria-controls), or promote the flyout to a real menu pattern with roving tabindex. Apply to both admin and portal sidebars.

findings.title: Notification bell and store drawer toggles omit aria-expanded
evidence: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:196-206 — the bell <button aria-label="Notifications (N unread)"> has no aria-expanded although it toggles the panel at :221-222
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:147-154 — the panel closes only on outside mousedown; no Escape handler

apps/web/components/store/StoreLayoutShell.tsx:31-36 — the mobile 'Browse categories' toggle has aria-label but no aria-expanded, unlike the equivalent components/layout/SidebarShell.tsx:79-80 which sets aria-expanded={drawerOpen}
findings.impact: Screen-reader users cannot tell whether the notifications panel or store drawer is open; the bell is present on every portal/admin page.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-expanded to both toggles (and Escape-to-close plus focus return for the bell panel), matching the SidebarShell pattern.

findings.title: Color-token drift: 66 files hardcode hex colors (80x #0A1118) and 45 arbitrary rgba card backgrounds instead of the design tokens
evidence: grep over apps/web/app + apps/web/components: 66 of 510 tsx files contain a hardcoded 6-digit hex; most frequent #0A1118 (80), #10b981 (30), #f59e0b (14), #059669 (10)

Examples: text-[#0A1118] on primary buttons (components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:707, app/(admin)/admin/store/audit/StoreAuditClient.tsx:54) where the token colors.cyber.base is already exposed as cyber-base by apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:14-18
45 arbitrary card backgrounds (bg-[rgba(18,30,45,0.75)] x15, bg-[rgba(18,30,45,0.5)] x27, ...) duplicate packages/ui/src/styles.css:36-42 glass-card/cyber-card values
Tokens exist and are wired: packages/ui/src/tokens/colors.ts:1-13, semantic-colors.ts:3-16, apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:2-40
findings.impact: The recent contrast fix (commit f0d79194) had to edit individual button classes rather than one token; future palette or contrast changes require mass edits and will miss sites. Design-system drift undermines the otherwise well-tuned palette.
findings.recommendation: Replace hardcoded values with the existing utilities (text-cyber-base, glass-card, bg-cyber-card-*) in touched files, and add a lint/regex guard that rejects new hex colors in apps/web/app and apps/web/components outside the token files.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. Note the palette itself passes contrast checks (see body) — this is a consistency finding, not a contrast finding.

findings.title: Heading order skips a level on the store import/export page
evidence: apps/web/components/admin/AdminPageShell.tsx:27 renders the page <h1>
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/store/import-export/ImportExportClient.tsx:168,193,220,239,259 — the five section headings are <h3> with no intervening <h2>
axe heading-order is a moderate rule and apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:99-101 filters to critical/serious, so the gate cannot catch it; /admin/store/import-export is also not in the a11y page lists
findings.impact: Screen-reader heading navigation skips a level and the section outline is wrong. Low user impact, trivial fix.
findings.recommendation: Promote the section headings to <h2> (or add an <h2> group heading).
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. A repo-wide heading scan found this as the only h1->h3 skip; all other sampled pages are consistent.

findings.title: ScorecardsEvaluateClient renders the only programmatically unlabeled input in the app and an unannounced error
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/edu-automation/scorecards/ScorecardsEvaluateClient.tsx:35-40 — <input> with only placeholder="Org UUID (blank = all orgs)", no <label>, no aria-label, not wrapped in a label
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/edu-automation/scorecards/ScorecardsEvaluateClient.tsx:49 — {error && {error}} with no role=alert
A full-app scan (attribute-aware, excluding labels and hidden inputs) found this as the single unlabeled form control across 510 tsx files
findings.impact: The input is announced without a name; the failure message is silent to AT. Everything else in the app is labeled, so this is a single-file cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Add aria-label="Organization ID (optional)" or a visible <label>, and role="alert" on the error span.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d. The same scan found zero icon-only buttons without accessible names, so this is an isolated gap.

findings.title: Signup form inputs lack autocomplete attributes
evidence: apps/web/app/(public)/signup/page.tsx:55 (fullName), :72 (email), :90 (password) — no autoComplete attribute on any of the three inputs
The login page does it correctly: apps/web/app/(public)/login/page.tsx:148 autoComplete="email", :168 autoComplete="current-password", :310 autoComplete="one-time-code"
grep for autoComplete across apps/web returns only login/page.tsx and MfaSettingsClient.tsx
findings.impact: WCAG 1.3.5 (Identify Input Purpose, AA) is not met on the signup form: password managers and AT input aids do not get the field-purpose hints that login already provides.
findings.recommendation: Add autoComplete="name", "email" and "new-password" to the signup fields.

findings.title: Storybook covers only the 7 @mct/ui primitives; packages/ui has no test/lint scripts and the a11y addon runs nowhere
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/*.stories.tsx — 7 story files (Avatar, Badge, Button, Dialog, Input, SidebarGroup, Skeleton)
find apps/web -name '*.stories.*' returns nothing, although .storybook/main.ts:6 globs '../apps/web/components/**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx)'
packages/ui/package.json has no "scripts" key at all (no test, lint or typecheck), and packages/ui contains no test files; turbo.json only runs tasks that exist per package

.storybook/main.ts:13 installs @storybook/addon-a11y and .storybook/preview.tsx:20-24 enables the color-contrast rule, but the only CI consumer (.github/workflows/chromatic.yml:22-28) is continue-on-error because the Storybook build fails (docs/CI.md:114-116)
No visual snapshot tests exist anywhere (no toHaveScreenshot/toMatchSnapshot usages)
findings.impact: The component library the design system depends on has no automated regression or accessibility safety net; app-level primitives (Chip, StatusPill, ConfirmDialog, EmptyState, drawer shells) are covered only indirectly by page tests. Cross-ref: CI-P2-006 and TEST-P3-001 (Chromatic/visual regression) are owned by the CI/testing domains.
findings.recommendation: Add stories for the app primitives, wire @storybook/test-runner or jest-axe assertions for the existing 7 components, add test/lint/typecheck scripts to packages/ui, and make Chromatic blocking once the webpack build failure is fixed.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; distinct from TEST-P3-001 (which covers the non-blocking visual-regression job itself) because it is about component coverage and the untested library.

findings.title: Full accessibility breadth scan (68 routes) is triage-only and not a required check
evidence: .github/workflows/a11y-breadth.yml:1-22 — scheduled (Mon 05:23) + manual workflow that calls e2e.yml with a11y_full: true; no continue-on-error key and no required-check wiring
apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:5-32 BASE_PAGES (25) run by the default E2E job, :37-81 FULL_PAGES (43), :83-86 selects the set from A11Y_FULL

.github/branch-protection/main.json:5-11 — required contexts are Test / test (20.x), Lint / lint (20.x), TypeCheck / typecheck, E2E / e2e (20.x), Dependency Review / review; the breadth workflow is not among them

docs/CI.md:21 and docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:90-93 document the breadth scan as triage-only; docs/CI.md:117 additionally claims the breadth job is continue-on-error: true, which a11y-breadth.yml does not set (doc/code mismatch)
Route inventory: 319 page.tsx files vs 68 scanned routes (~21%); the 43 breadth-only routes include /admin/store/*, /admin/webhooks*, /admin/governance, /portal/runbooks and others
findings.impact: Regressions on the 43 breadth-only routes (and any WCAG 2.2 rule added later) do not fail any required check; the doc mismatch makes the signal level hard to reason about.
findings.recommendation: Ratchet the breadth set into BASE_PAGES in batches (start with the routes that are currently clean), record a violation baseline, and fix docs/CI.md:117 or add continue-on-error deliberately. Prefer failing the weekly run visibly over silently passing.
findings.note: RE-VERIFIED at 8d299b8d (previous run mainecybertech-20261004-full-main-9c0b88c, status open, verified at 9c0b88c): the workflow is still schedule/manual, the default gate still scans 25 routes, and no branch-protection context references it — still triage-only. New residual: docs/CI.md:117 claims continue-on-error: true that .github/workflows/a11y-breadth.yml:17-22 does not set.

findings.title: The a11y gate scans only initial page loads; interactive states (dialogs, drawers, filters, bulk bars) and client-fetched content are untested
evidence: apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:89-111 — each test is goto -> waitForLoadState(domcontentloaded) -> waitForLoadState(networkidle, {timeout: 5000}).catch(() => {}) -> axe analyze; no click/hover/open interaction is performed
apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts:92-96 comment — the notification bell's EventSource can keep the connection busy, so the bounded networkidle wait is expected to fall through silently
Client-fetched pages are scanned whenever that bounded wait ends, e.g. components/NotificationsPageClient.tsx:50-60 fetches its list on mount and renders the empty/loading state until it resolves
None of the 14 role="dialog" components, the mobile drawers, the filter chips, or the ticket bulk-selection bar is exercised by the scan
findings.impact: Violations that exist only in opened dialogs/drawers, filtered states or post-fetch content are invisible to the gate — the same class as the ticket-card nesting above. Green gate results overstate WCAG confidence.
findings.recommendation: Add a small interaction suite (open each dialog/drawer, apply a filter chip, bulk-select a row, run axe in the open state) and/or jest-axe unit tests for the shared primitives; keep the bounded-wait fallback but log when it triggers.
findings.note: New finding at 8d299b8d; static review of the spec only — the 5s bounded wait usually gives client fetches time to complete, so the main gap is unexercised interactive states rather than empty-state scanning.

report:
# UI/UX, Design System, and Accessibility Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: `repo-deep-dive`
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `mainecybertech` (monorepo: `apps/web` Next.js App Router, `apps/api`, `apps/worker`, `packages/ui`, `packages/sdk`, `packages/config`)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8d` (`8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (read-only static review)
- Area code: UX
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/05_ui_ux_accessibility_audit.md`
- Scope limitations: **static JSX/CSS review only** — no browser, no axe run, no screenshots, no `pnpm install`/`build` (host is a 1 vCPU droplet). Contrast values were computed from the token hex values. No live accessibility-tree inspection. Findings that depend on runtime behavior (click bubbling, axe rule firing) are marked with their confidence.

## Scope

Reviewed at `8d299b8d`:

- `packages/ui` in full: tokens (`src/tokens/*`), `styles.css`, ThemeProvider/useTheme, and all 7 components (Button, Input/Textarea, Badge, Avatar, Dialog, Skeleton\*, SidebarGroup/Item) plus their 7 stories.
- `apps/web`: root/public/portal/admin layouts, `tailwind.config.ts`, `app/globals.css`, `components/**` (layout, marketing, store, portal, admin, ui), the shared shells/guards (`AdminPageShell`, `AdminListPage`, `ModuleDetailPage`, `RecordDetail`, `ConfirmDialog`, `SubmitButton`, `RouteGuard`, `EmptyState`, `DataErrorNote`, `Breadcrumbs`, `ToastProvider`, `RouteAnnouncer`), the a11y E2E spec, Storybook config and the Chromatic workflow.
- Process evidence: `docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/ui-kit.md`, `docs/CI.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.github/branch-protection/main.json`.
- Previous run artifacts for the verification duty: `runs/mainecybertech-20261004-full-main-9c0b88c/follow_up_register.md` (UX-P3-001).

Not reviewed: `apps/api` UI-adjacent behavior, email templates, PDF generation, native app surfaces (none), and any runtime rendering (no server/browser available).

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `packages/ui/src/tokens/{colors,semantic-colors,focus,typography,spacing,borders,shadows,motion}.ts` | Source | Design-token definitions | Complete, typed, exported |
| `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:1-43` | Config | Token → Tailwind wiring | Imports colors/spacing/typography/borders/shadows/motion; **not** semantic-colors/focus |
| `packages/ui/src/styles.css` | Source | Global utilities, focus-visible, reduced motion, dark/light vars | 183 lines; global `*:focus-visible` outline |
| `packages/ui/src/components/*.tsx` + `*.stories.tsx` | Source | Shared component library | 7 components, 7 stories |
| `apps/web/app/layout.tsx`, `(public)/layout.tsx`, `(portal)/layout.tsx`, `(admin)/admin/layout.tsx` | Source | Landmarks, skip link, providers | `#main-content` present in both shells |
| `apps/web/components/**` (≈300 files) | Source | Component consistency, ARIA, forms, tables, dialogs | Scanned by attribute-aware scripts |
| `apps/web/e2e/a11y.spec.ts` | Test | WCAG gate (25 routes) + breadth triage (68) | axe-core critical/serious filter |
| `.storybook/{main.ts,preview.tsx}`, `.github/workflows/chromatic.yml` | Config/CI | Storybook + visual regression | a11y addon configured; job `continue-on-error` |
| `apps/web/__tests__/**` (≈250 files) | Test | Role-based query usage | 460 `*ByRole` queries, no jest-axe |
| `docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md`, `docs/ui-kit.md` | Docs | The declared standard | 93 + ~200 lines |
| `docs/CI.md:13,21,115-119`, `docs/testing.md:66-68` | Docs | A11y/CI process claims | Used for verification |
| `.github/branch-protection/main.json` | Config | Required checks | E2E required; breadth scan not |
| Previous register `…9c0b88c/follow_up_register.md:342` (UX-P3-001) | Prior finding | Verification duty | Re-checked |

## Verification Performed

All commands were read-only against `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target` at `8d299b8d`.

## Executive Summary

The UI layer is in better shape than a 500-component app usually is. Accessibility is treated as a first-class concern: a skip link and `#main-content` landmark on every shell, a global `:focus-visible` outline that cannot be defeated by utility `outline-none` classes, a global `prefers-reduced-motion` block plus JS respect in the particle canvas, a deliberately contrast-tuned slate palette (all sampled combos ≥ 4.5:1), 14/14 dialogs with `aria-modal` + focus trap + Escape + focus restore, a route announcer for client navigation, a well-built toast system with polite/assertive regions, labelled form controls almost everywhere (1 miss in 510 files), 0 nameless icon-only buttons, 0 nested-link/button patterns except one, and a 25-route axe gate wired into the required E2E check.

The gaps are concentrated in **verification breadth and component consistency**, not in fundamentals:

1. **Interactive states are outside the gate.** The axe scan only loads pages; dialogs, drawers, filter chips and bulk-selection bars are never scanned. The one nested-interactive defect found by static review (`AdminTicketCenterClient`) is exactly the kind the gate cannot see — and it also breaks mouse multi-select.
2. **Feedback is silent for AT.** ~44 components render async action errors as plain red text with no live region, contradicting the project's own convention (`docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:51-52`).
3. **Modal responsiveness is inconsistent.** Some dialogs handle small viewports; five do not, including a 10-field promotion form and the shared `@mct/ui` Dialog.
4. **The design system is bypassed.** `@mct/ui` interactive primitives are used in 7 files; the app hand-rolls 234 raw button classes and four identical Chip copies. Tokens are also bypassed (66 files hardcode hex colors).
5. **89 pages have no specific title** (WCAG 2.4.2, Level A), and the breadth scan that would catch new route-level regressions is still triage-only (previous UX-P3-001).

No P0/P1 was found in this domain: nothing blocks a release, but items 1–3 should be fixed before the next broad rollout of the admin surfaces.

## Detailed Review

### Item: Design tokens and theme

- Evidence: `packages/ui/src/tokens/*.ts`, `apps/web/tailwind.config.ts:2-40`, `packages/ui/src/styles.css:5-13,153-165`, `docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md:83`.
- What it does: tokens define the cyber palette, spacing, type, radii, shadows and motion; Tailwind consumes six token groups; `styles.css` exposes `cyber-*` utilities and CSS variables.
- How it appears to work: components use Tailwind utilities generated from tokens (plus remapped slate shades for contrast); arbitrary values are used freely where tokens exist.
- Missing controls: no guard against new hardcoded colors; `semanticColors` and `focus` tokens are exported but referenced nowhere; the light-theme block and ThemeProvider branches are unreachable.
- Risks: drift, mass-edit cost, misleading Storybook theme toolbar.
- Recommended improvement: adopt `text-cyber-base`/`glass-card` in touched files, delete dead theme paths (or implement a toggle), add a hex-color guard.
- Suggested tests: a regex/ESLint check for `#[0-9a-f]{6}` in `apps/web/{app,components}`; a Storybook story that asserts `data-theme` handling if a toggle is added.
- Suggested docs: update `docs/WEB_UI_CONVENTIONS.md` (“Consistency”) with the token-vs-hex rule.

### Item: Shared primitives (`@mct/ui`)

- Evidence: `packages/ui/src/index.ts:14-21`; usage counts (Button 6 files, Input/Dialog/Badge 1, others 0); 234 raw `cyber-button*` usages; Chip ×4; `packages/ui/package.json` has no scripts.
- What it does: provides Button/Input/Badge/Avatar/Dialog/Skeleton/Sidebar primitives with loading, error, focus and ARIA handling.
- How it appears to work: only auth pages and `DocumentShareClient` import interactive primitives; the rest of the app uses `cyber-*` classes and local copies.
- Missing controls: no lint rule, no ownership doc beyond `docs/ui-kit.md`, no tests for the library.
- Risks: a11y fixes applied per call site; duplicated behavior drift (e.g. StoreLayoutShell vs SidebarShell `aria-expanded`).
- Recommended improvement: single standard; move Chip/ConfirmDialog/StatusPill into `@mct/ui`; add scripts + jest-axe.
- Suggested tests: RTL + jest-axe tests for each primitive; Storybook test-runner.
- Suggested docs: `docs/ui-kit.md` “which one to use” decision table; deprecation note for raw `cyber-button*`.

### Item: Modals and drawers

- Evidence: 14 `role="dialog"` with `aria-modal`; `useFocusTrap` in 10 files + SidebarShell trap; good scroll patterns in `ProductForm.tsx:85`, `AdminProjectsClient.tsx:305`, `AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:718`; missing in `PromoForm.tsx:60-71`, `CategoryForm.tsx:52-63`, `SupportCenterClient.tsx:216-225`, `AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx:1769-1780`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx:37-47`, `Dialog.tsx:114-119`.
- What it does: consistent dialog semantics; inconsistent viewport handling.
- Risks: clipped forms/unreachable submit on small screens.
- Recommended improvement: fix the shared Dialog + the four app modals; add a viewport test.
- Suggested tests: Playwright at 375×667 opening each modal and asserting the primary button is visible/clickable.

### Item: Forms and feedback

- Evidence: 1 unlabeled input in 510 files; ContactForm exemplary (`ContactForm.tsx:117-289`); Input component wires `aria-invalid`/`aria-describedby`; 44 files render errors without live regions; signup lacks `autocomplete`.
- Recommended improvement: InlineError primitive; autocomplete on auth forms.
- Suggested tests: RTL test asserting `role="alert"` appears after a failed submit; a lint/scan test for unlabeled controls.

### Item: Tables, lists and navigation

- Evidence: 22 files with tables, all in scroll wrappers, `scope` used 102×; no `aria-sort` (sorting is via selects); `AdminPagination` has `nav[aria-label]` + `aria-current`; breadcrumbs are `nav > ol`.
- Recommended improvement: none required; consider `<caption class="sr-only">` for data tables and `aria-sort` if sortable headers are introduced.

### Item: Motion, icons and color

- Evidence: global reduced-motion block (`styles.css:174-183`); `ParticleBackground.tsx:59` checks `prefers-reduced-motion`; lucide icons with `aria-hidden` on decorative SVGs; contrast computed for 12 combos, all pass.
- Recommended improvement: replace `text-[10px]`/`text-[11px]` micro-type where it carries meaning; keep contrast discipline.

### Finding UX-P2-001 — Ticket-card bulk selection nests a checkbox and a status button inside a Link

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: UX
- Evidence: `apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:191-192` (whole card is a `<Link>`); `:197-204` (checkbox inside it, `handleCheckboxChange` at `:184-187` stops only `change`); `:218-221` (status button inside it calls `preventDefault`+`stopPropagation` via `:172-177`); `:551-574` (header select-all sits in a plain label outside any Link).
- What is happening: the per-row checkbox is nested inside an anchor; the click that selects the row also bubbles to the Link, so selection navigates to the detail page. The sibling status button is explicitly guarded, showing the wrapper is known to be interactive.
- Why it matters: invalid interactive nesting (axe `nested-interactive`, serious, medium confidence it fires) and a broken bulk-select workflow.
- Recommended fix: move controls out of the Link (title-only link / stretched-link pattern) or intercept the click; add a regression test.
- Owner suggestion: web UI engineer (admin tickets) · Effort: S · Target: this month · Status: open.

- Severity: P2 · Confidence: high · Area: UX
